user.title: Set up ELRO Connects K2
user.description: Searching for ELRO Connects K2 gateways on the local network...

pick.title: Choose a gateway
pick.description: {count} ELRO Connects K2 gateways were found that are not set up yet. Each hub is a separate installation with its own detectors, so add them one at a time — run this again to add the next.

confirm.title: ELRO Connects K2 found
confirm.description: Found K2 gateway at {host} (ID: {device_name}). Add it to Home Assistant?

manual.title: Manual setup
manual.description: Enter the gateway's IP address and device name. The device name is shown in the ELRO Connects app under connector › settings › Connector details › device name, and must match exactly — a hub called by the wrong name ignores Home Assistant completely.

error.cannot_connect: No K2 gateway at that address answered to that device name. Check both: the name must match the hub exactly, the hub must be reachable, and UDP port 1025 must be open in both directions.

abort.already_configured: This K2 gateway is already configured.

hub_not_armed.title: ELRO Connects K2 hub {device_name} is not responding
hub_not_armed.description:
The hub at **{host}** never acknowledged an activation ping, so it is ignoring every command Home Assistant sends it and no devices could be created.

The usual causes are a wrong IP address or device name, UDP port 1025 being blocked or already in use, or a firewall silently dropping the hub's outbound internet traffic, which stalls the hub and stops it answering locally until that attempt times out — use a *reject* rule rather than a *drop* rule if you block it.

See the troubleshooting guide linked below, or switch on debug logging in the integration options to see every frame. This notification clears itself once the hub reports a device.

hub_not_answering.title: ELRO Connects K2 hub {device_name} is not answering commands
hub_not_answering.description:
The hub at **{host}** is on the network and replies to Home Assistant's activation pings, but it answers no command at all — not even a request for its own settings, which does not depend on what is paired with it. So the hub is reachable and is not processing what Home Assistant sends it.

That points at the hub or the network rather than at anything configured here. Worth trying, cheapest first: power-cycle the hub; move it closer to its access point; and check whether anything is silently dropping the hub's outbound internet traffic. A *drop* rule leaves the hub retransmitting until its own timeout expires and it stops answering locally in the meantime — use a *reject* rule instead if you block it. Intrusion prevention, DNS filtering and country blocking each sit outside ordinary firewall rules and can all cause this.

See the troubleshooting guide linked below, or switch on debug logging in the integration options to see every frame. This notification clears itself once the hub reports a device.

hub_no_devices.title: ELRO Connects K2 hub {device_name} reports no devices
hub_no_devices.description:
The hub at **{host}** is answering Home Assistant normally — it replied to a request for its own settings, which does not depend on what is paired with it — and then listed no detectors, so no entities could be created. The hub is working; it reports that nothing is paired with it.

Check the ELRO Connects app to see which detectors it shows for this hub. If the app lists detectors that Home Assistant does not, note that the app can show them from its own cache or from the ELRO cloud rather than from the hub itself, so that alone does not mean the hub still has them — re-pairing a detector is what puts it back in the hub's own list.

See the troubleshooting guide linked below, or switch on debug logging in the integration options to see every frame. This notification clears itself once the hub reports a device.

start_pairing.name: Add device
start_pairing.description: Puts the K2 gateway into pairing mode and waits for a new detector to join. Trigger the detector's pairing action (usually by holding its test button) while this is running. The detector type does not need to be selected - the gateway accepts whichever device joins.

config_entry_id.name: Gateway
config_entry_id.description: Which K2 gateway to pair with. Can be left empty when only one is set up.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long to keep pairing mode open while waiting for a detector to join.

cancel_pairing.name: Cancel adding device
cancel_pairing.description: Closes an open pairing window on the K2 gateway before it times out.

config_entry_id.name: Gateway
config_entry_id.description: Which K2 gateway to stop pairing on. Can be left empty when only one is set up.
